cards.text: Israel just lost the battle, and the Philistines captured the ark of God. Now they carry it from Ebenezer to Ashdod, one of their cities. Friend, they think they just won the prize of the war. They have NO idea what they're holding.

cards.question: In Ashdod, the Philistines carry the ark into the temple of their god ___ and set it beside his statue.
The ark sits beside Dagon's statue all night. When the people of Ashdod get up early the next morning, what do they find?

answers.text: Dagon fallen on his face before the ark
The ark carried out of the temple
Dagon's statue cracked down the middle

cards.question: After finding Dagon on his face, the people of Ashdod leave him lying there on the floor.

cards.text: They pick Dagon up and put him right back in his place. Friend, I dove face-first into the chocolate chips just last week, but at least I got back up BY MYSELF.

cards.question: The next morning, there's Dagon on his face before the ark of the LORD again. What's different this time?

answers.text: His head and hands are broken off
He is lying outside the temple doors

cards.text: Day one, Dagon falls down. Day two... he falls APART, with his head and hands lying on the threshold and only the torso left.

cards.question: Because of what happened, the priests of Dagon and everyone who enters his temple in Ashdod don't step on the threshold, even to this day.
Now the hand of the LORD is heavy on the people of Ashdod and the area around it. He ravages them and afflicts them with ___.
The men of Ashdod see what's happening to their city. What do they decide?

answers.text: The ark must not stay with them
Dagon must move to a new temple
They must bring more gifts to Dagon

cards.text: Their reason: "His hand is heavy upon us and upon our god Dagon." Two face-plants and a lot of tumors later, they finally put it together.

cards.question: The men of Ashdod call together all the rulers of the Philistines and ask what to do with the ark. Where do the rulers say to move it?
The ark moves to Gath, and the LORD's hand is against that city too, throwing it into great confusion. In Gath, only the old men get tumors.

cards.text: So they send the ark on to Ekron. Friend, this is a burning-hot cookie sheet and NOBODY has an oven mitt: pass it, pass it, PASS IT!

cards.question: The ark of the God of Israel arrives in Ekron. What do the Ekronites cry out?

answers.text: It was brought here to kill us
It will bring our city great honor
It belongs beside our own god now

cards.question: The Ekronites call together all the rulers of the Philistines. They say to send the ark away so it can return to ___.

cards.text: A deadly confusion fills Ekron, and the hand of God is very heavy on it. Those who don't die are afflicted with tumors.

cards.question: The people of Ekron cry out, and the outcry of the city goes up to ___.

cards.text: That's where we set it down for now, friend. But trust me, this ark's story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences. The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: "Israel just lost the battle" is a fact from 1 Samuel 4:10, outside the passage. The card gives no reference for it and cites only 1 Samuel 5:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "They think they just won the prize of the war" states what the Philistines think as fact. The text doesn't say this, and the line isn't marked as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "The ark carried out of the temple" happens later in the passage: the ark is carried away from Ashdod to Gath in 5:8. A baker could argue it's true.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He is lying outside the temple doors" is close to the right detail. In 5:4, Dagon's head and hands lie on the threshold, which is the temple doorway, so a baker could argue it.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The right answer "its place" is a different kind of thing from the wrong answers "Gath" and "Ashdod", which are city names. It is also two words while they are one. The Ekronites wouldn't want the ark sent back to cities it already struck, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "Gath" and "Ashdod" don't fit a cry going "up to" somewhere. Next to them, "heaven" stands out as the only answer that makes sense.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line nearly copies the doc's example ("And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.") instead of being a fresh line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: This last story card is only the story-isn't-over line and tells nothing from 1 Samuel 5:12. It still cites 1 Samuel 5:12.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-isn't-over line and tells no verse, what should its "verses" field cite: the passage's last verse, the whole passage, or nothing?
